text: Do this for every method, and you get an atlas. The paper reads seven coordinates off each method's formula: where it acts; the shape of its image; where it starts, at a tip, a smooth point, or off target; its gauge; which changes of basis it respects; whether it can be merged; and what merge-and-restart can reach. <short pause> Three hundred and eighty-two methods from a hundred and thirty-eight papers. Four hundred and three arrows saying which method simulates which, each with an explicit map, and four hundred and eighty-five obstructions saying which can't.
